Watch these full remarks from yesterday's bill signing. #NYSafetyAgenda

@ItsMichelleHurd: “Today was made possible because we turned pain into action & passed a law that will take us one step further to a future where not one more person will ever have to say #MeToo again.” https://t.co/acb96z2b7J

Day 1: @ItsMichelleHurd. Her advocacy helped to pass the #NYSafetyAgenda, giving NY rape survivors more time to seek justice.

"We turned pain into action & passed a law that will take us one step further to a future where not one more person will ever have to say #MeToo again.” https://t.co/ATryioxDkv

“The outpouring of #MeToo stories has really revealed how inadequate our laws have been for way too long."

But we're making progress -- since 2017, 15 states have revised or introduced protections for everyday workers. cc @nwlc (#TIMESUP x @nowthisnews) https://t.co/oMb7wUpcti

Big news for CA! Thank you @GavinNewsom for signing 2 important #MeToo bills:

#AB51 - #EndForcedArbitration
#AB9 - More time to file a claim

Major thanks to @EqualRightsAdv @MiraSorvino @LiliBernard @_jessicabarth_ & many others who fought for this win. https://t.co/vqWQw4sZCq

This week marks the 2nd anniversary of the #MeToo hashtag and the start of a monumental shift. It was a consciousness-stirring moment, but creating awareness alone is not enough. 

So we demand more - we're ready to vote for accountability. #MeTooVoter https://t.co/ikC35tXzxU

We’re halfway through the 4th #DemDebate, on the two year anniversary of the #metoo hashtag, rooted in @TaranaBurke's work.

Yet we’ve heard zero questions on sexual violence in any 2019 primary debate. We've heard zero questions in at least two decades. #MeTooVoter #TIMESUP2020

@TIMESUPLDF @salmahayek @chadbatka @nytimes @Jacquelyn_M @AP @PGannawayPhoto @BuzzFeed @Lupita_Nyongo @jessedittmar @gdemczuk @teamcoworker @PadmaLakshmi @Godbold @EchoTrainingOrg @THR “I feel a connection, because what they suffered, I suffered in my own flesh. I feel proud of them & of myself...I had the courage to lift my voice.”

Paula chose to speak because of the many who came forward to say #MeToo. (📷 Debee Tlumacki @BostonGlobe) https://t.co/uBIOWVy8Eq https://t.co/6MqhXRRV0A

There has been “historic progress—but there needs to be action to sustain it. And one important stakeholder who has the power to build on the #metoo progress is the business community.” - Esta Soler, @WithoutViolence https://t.co/MEVtJBSN16

In a historic move, @kwelkernbc has asked a presidential candidate about #MeToo and sexual violence.

Sending gratitude to every survivor who came forward and spoke out. Without them, this moment would have never been possible. #MeTooVoter #TIMESUP2020
